mainTopic: How ה׳ judges: the sun in the future, the fear of government, ה׳'s gentle punishment of ישראל, the righteous and the wicked, and the moment of ה׳'s anger
overview: This amud finishes a teaching from the previous daf: in the future the sun will burn the wicked and heal and refresh the righteous. The גמרא then explains that people are like fish, because without fear of the government the strong would swallow the weak, and a משנה in אבות says to pray for the government's welfare. Next come several pairs of פסוקים that seem to clash: about ה׳'s power (hidden in judgment, shown in war) and about His fury (held back from ישראל, shown to the nations). A series of teachings explains that ה׳ punishes ישראל little by little, like a hen pecking, and uses loss of money and suffering in this world to earn them עולם הבא. In a story, the מינים torment רב ספרא when he cannot explain a פסוק in עמוס, and רבי אבהו answers them with a parable of a lender who collects from a friend little by little but from an enemy all at once. רבי אבא בר כהנא teaches that killing the righteous with the wicked would be a desecration. The גמרא explains that only people who are not completely righteous, including those who could have protested sin and did not, are punished with the wicked. Finally, ה׳'s daily anger is explained: a community can withstand it, and it lasts only a tiny רגע, which only בלעם could pinpoint. The פסוק about בלעם comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The wicked are judged by the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the statement that in the future the wicked will be punished by the sun. It brings a פסוק from מלאכי as the source and explains 'root' and 'branch.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The wicked are judged by the sun, as the פסוק says: 'For behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace, and all the proud and all who do evil will be like straw, and the coming day will set them on fire, says ה׳ of hosts, so that it leaves them neither root nor branch.' No root means nothing left in this world, and no branch means nothing in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began on the previous page: the wicked will be judged by the sun. It proves this from a פסוק that describes a day 'burning like a furnace.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'burning day' in the פסוק is read as the sun, which will burn the wicked. The words 'root' and 'branch' are each given a meaning. Root stands for this world and branch stands for עולם הבא, so the wicked lose both.

keyTerms.meaning: Wicked people (the subject of this sentence, which started on the previous page)

phrases.english: by it, as it is written:
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf: the wicked are judged by 'it', meaning the sun.

phrases.english: "For behold, the day comes,
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:19. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: burning like a furnace,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ כׇל זֵדִים וְכׇל עֹשֵׂה רִשְׁעָה קַשׁ
phrases.english: and all the proud and all who do wickedness shall be straw,
and the coming day shall set them on fire,
says ה׳ of hosts,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲזֹב לָהֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ וְעָנָף״,
phrases.english: so that it shall leave them neither root nor branch."
No root: in this world,
and no branch: in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching from the previous daf about the sun in the future
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future the wicked will be burned by the sun and lose both this world and עולם הבא.

steps.title: The righteous are healed and refreshed by the sun
steps.stepSummary: The same sun that burns the wicked will heal the righteous, and it will even make them feel new and full of life. Both points come from the next פסוק in מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The righteous are healed by it, as the פסוק says: 'But for you who fear My Name, a sun of righteousness will shine, with healing in its wings.' And not only that, they will also be refreshed by it, as it says: 'And you will go out and leap like calves from the stall.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the other half of the teaching: the righteous will be healed by the same sun. It adds that they will also be refreshed and full of joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. First, 'healing in its wings' shows the righteous are healed. Then the phrase 'leap like calves' adds that they will feel young and full of energy, which is more than just being cured.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
Fattened calves kept in a stall

phrases.english: The righteous are healed by it, as it is written:
"But for you who fear My Name will shine
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:20

phrases.english: a sun of righteousness
with healing in its wings, etc."
And not only that, but they are even refreshed by it,
as it is said: "And you will go out and leap
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: like calves from the stall."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite result of the same sun: healing instead of burning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun that burns the wicked will heal and refresh the righteous.
steps.whatToRemember: The same sun brings two opposite results. It burns the wicked and heals and refreshes the righteous.

steps.title: Another reason people are like fish: the strong swallow the weak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another explanation of why people are compared to fish. Bigger fish swallow smaller ones, and people would do the same if they did not fear the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as with fish in the sea, the bigger one swallows the smaller one, so too with people. If not for the fear of the government, whoever is bigger than another would swallow him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the comparison of people to fish from the previous page and gives a new explanation of it. Without a government that people fear, the strong would destroy the weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanations compared people to fish in other ways. This one is about how society works. People act like fish, and the fear of the government is the only thing that stops the bigger from swallowing the smaller.

phrases.english: Another explanation: just as with fish of the sea,
phrases.notes: Another reason why the פסוק 'ותעשה אדם כדגי הים' (חבקוק 1:14) compares people to fish.

phrases.english: whichever is bigger than the other
swallows the other,
so too people:
if not for the fear of the government,
whoever is bigger than the other
would swallow the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the fish comparison from the previous daf and gives an alternative explanation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the fear of the government, stronger people would destroy weaker people, the way big fish swallow small ones.

steps.title: Support from the משנה of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this idea matches a משנה in אבות. There רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים tells people to pray for the government's welfare, because without fear of it people would swallow each other alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned in a משנה: רבי חנינא, the assistant to the כהן גדול, says: Pray for the welfare of the government, because if not for the fear of the government, people would swallow each other alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the fish idea with a משנה that says the same thing in almost the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the very same picture of swallowing a neighbor alive. This shows the 'fish' explanation agrees with an accepted teaching. The משנה also adds a practical lesson: pray that the government stays strong.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what we learned in a משנה
For the welfare of the government

phrases.english: And this is what we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: The משנה is in אבות 3:2.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant to the High Priest, says:
Pray for the welfare of the government,
because if not for the fear of the government,
"each man would swallow his neighbor alive."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 with a matching משנה
steps.raayaObject: The idea that fear of the government stops people from swallowing each other
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in אבות 3:2, from רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
steps.whatToRemember: Fear of the government keeps society safe, so a person should pray for its welfare.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice of praying for the welfare of the government.

steps.title: פסוקים that seem to contradict each other about ה׳'s power
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר פפא points out a contradiction. One פסוק says we cannot find ה׳'s great power, while two others praise His great power openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר פפא pointed out a contradiction. One פסוק says: 'The Almighty, we have not found Him great in power.' But another says: 'Great is our Lord and mighty in power,' and another says: 'Your right hand, ה׳, is glorious in power'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב חיננא בר פפא sets פסוקים against each other because they seem to disagree about whether ה׳'s power is seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב suggests ה׳ does not show His power. The פסוקים in תהלים and שמות describe His power as great and visible. Both cannot seem true at once, so an answer is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (literally, 'throws' one against another)

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Pappa pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "The Almighty, we have not found Him great in power,"
phrases.notes: איוב 37:23

phrases.english: and it is written: "Great is our Lord and mighty in power,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 147:5

phrases.english: and it is written: "Your right hand, ה׳, is glorious in power"!
phrases.notes: שמות 15:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in איוב that says ה׳'s power is not found
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other פסוקים clearly describe ה׳'s power as great and seen, which seems to contradict איוב.

steps.title: Judgment time versus war time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוקים speak about different times. When ה׳ judges, He holds back His power. When He fights His enemies, His power is shown.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here it speaks about a time of judgment, and there it speaks about a time of war.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each פסוק is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a time of judgment, ה׳ acts with mercy and does not use His full strength, so 'we have not found Him great in power.' At a time of war against His enemies, His great power is shown, as the other פסוקים describe. Both are true, just at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source refers to a different case)

phrases.english: It is not a problem:
here it speaks of a time of judgment,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק in איוב, where ה׳ holds back His power.

phrases.english: there it speaks of a time of war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק refers to a different time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seemed to disagree about whether ה׳'s power is seen.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳'s power is held back in judgment and shown in war.
steps.whatToRemember: When the גמרא says 'כאן... כאן', it settles a contradiction by showing that each source talks about a different situation.

steps.title: Two verses disagree about ה׳'s fury
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא shows that one פסוק says ה׳ has no fury, while another says He is full of fury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא points out a contradiction. One פסוק says, "Fury is not in Me." Another פסוק says, "ה׳ avenges and is full of fury."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It puts two פסוקים side by side that seem to say opposite things about ה׳'s anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו says ה׳ has no fury at all. נחום calls ה׳ a בעל חמה, someone full of fury. Both cannot be true in the same way, so something needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction (literally, 'throws' two sources against each other)
Full of fury, a master of anger

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina raises a contradiction:
It is written: "Fury is not in Me,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:4

phrases.english: and it is written: "ה׳ avenges and is full of fury"!
phrases.notes: נחום 1:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new contradiction between פסוקים, built the same way as the one in Step 5 about ה׳'s power.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים in ישעיהו and נחום about ה׳'s fury.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק denies ה׳ has fury, the other says He is full of it.

steps.title: No fury toward ישראל, fury toward the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק with no fury is about ישראל, and the פסוק with fury is about the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. One פסוק is talking about ישראל, and the other is talking about the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each פסוק speaks about a different group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ holds back His fury from ישראל, so "fury is not in Me" is about them. Toward the nations His fury is shown, so "full of fury" is about them. Both פסוקים are true, just about different people.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real problem
Here... there; each source refers to a different case

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about ישראל,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק "Fury is not in Me."

phrases.english: there, it is about the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן — בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כָּאן — בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different subjects: each פסוק refers to a different group.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seem to describe ה׳ in two opposite ways in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ holds back His fury from ישראל but shows it to the nations.

steps.title: No fury only because of an oath
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר פפא reads "Fury is not in Me" to mean ה׳ holds back only because He already swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר פפא says: "Fury is not in Me" because I already swore. "Would that I" had not sworn; then "I would be like briers and thorns" set on fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא בר פפא gives a different way to read the פסוק "Fury is not in Me," by looking at the words that follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק goes on: "Would that I were like briers and thorns." He reads it as: I have no fury only because I already swore; if I had not sworn, I would burn like fire. So ה׳'s fury is held back by a promise, not because it is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: I swore, I took an oath
Would that I; if only I could
Briers and thorns, which burn quickly

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Pappa said:
"Fury is not in Me" — because I already swore,
phrases.notes: The oath is understood to be ה׳'s promise not to destroy ישראל.

phrases.english: "Would that I" — had not sworn,
"I would be as briers and thorns, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the פסוק "Fury is not in Me" from the one in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ holds back His fury from ישראל because of His oath; without it, He would burn like fire.

steps.title: ה׳ checks the nations' records for merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי explains that before destroying the nations, ה׳ searches their records for any merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רבי אלכסנדרי said. The פסוק says, "On that day I will seek to destroy all the nations." Seek from whom? ה׳ says: I will search their records. If they have merit, I will save them. If not, I will destroy them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אלכסנדרי that matches the idea of how ה׳ judges the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "I will seek" sounds strange, as if ה׳ needs to ask someone. רבי אלכסנדרי explains it means ה׳ searches the nations' records first. Even when ה׳ judges the nations, He looks for a reason to save them before destroying them.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said; this matches another teaching
I will seek, I will search
I will redeem them, save them

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Alexandri said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And it shall be on that day
I will seek to destroy all the nations"?
phrases.notes: זכריה 12:9

phrases.english: "I will seek" from whom?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I will search in their records,
if they have merit, I will redeem them,
and if not, I will destroy them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a teaching that fits the theme of how ה׳ judges the nations.
steps.raayaObject: The idea of how ה׳ judges the nations, discussed in Steps 8-9.

steps.title: ה׳ punishes ישראל like a hen pecking
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ה׳ punishes the nations all at once, but punishes ישראל a little at a time, like a hen pecking.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רבא said about the פסוק "Surely He will not stretch out His hand into a ruin, though in his calamity they cry out." ה׳ told ישראל: When I judge you, I do not judge you like the nations, about whom it says "A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it." Rather, I punish you like the pecking of a hen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's teaching, which shows that ה׳ judges ישראל differently from the nations. This matches the answer in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the word בְּפִידוֹ as כְּפִיד, "pecking." The nations are punished in one big blow, like the triple "ruin" in יחזקאל. ישראל are punished in small bits, like a hen picking up tiny pieces, so they are never wiped out.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'in his calamity'; here read as 'pecking'
Like the pecking of a hen, a tiny bit at a time

phrases.english: And this is what Rava said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Surely He will not stretch out a hand into a ruin,
though in his calamity they cry out"?
phrases.notes: איוב 30:24. רבא will read בְּפִידוֹ as "pecking."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to ישראל:
When I judge ישראל,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֲנִי דָּן אוֹתָם כְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: I do not judge them like the nations of the world,
as it is written: "A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it, etc."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 21:32

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲנִי נִפְרָע מֵהֶן כְּפִיד שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: rather, I punish them like the pecking of a hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching that fits the theme; it backs up the difference between ישראל and the nations from Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The answer in Step 8 that ה׳ treats ישראל differently from the nations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's reading of איוב 30:24, contrasted with יחזקאל 21:32.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a clear picture of the difference from Step 8: ישראל are punished bit by bit, so they are never destroyed all at once.

steps.title: Small מצוות added into a big total
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of the same פסוק: even if ישראל do only a few מצוות‎, ה׳ adds them up into a large sum.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: Even if ישראל do only a few מצוות before Me, like hens pecking in a garbage heap, I will add them together into a big total, as it says, "Though by pecking, they are saved."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the same פסוק in איוב. Now the "pecking" is about ישראל's מצוות, not their punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the hen's pecking stands for doing only small bits of good. ה׳ collects all those little מצוות into one big account. So the פסוק now means: even with small pecks of מצוות, they are saved.

keyTerms.meaning: I combine them, add them together
A big total, a large account

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין מִצְוָה לְפָנַי
phrases.english: even if ישראל do not do מצוות before Me
except a little,
like the pecking of hens that peck in a garbage heap,
I will add them together into a big total,
as it is said: "Though by pecking, they are saved,"
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Here שׁוּעַ is read as "salvation."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין מִצְוָה לְפָנַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different reading of the same פסוק from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ adds up even small מצוות of ישראל into a large account that saves them.

steps.title: Saved because they cry out
steps.stepSummary: A third reading of the same פסוק‎: ה׳ saves ישראל as a reward for crying out to Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: As a reward for crying out before Me, I will save them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more reading of the words "לָהֶן שׁוּעַ" in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now שׁוּעַ is read as "crying out" in prayer. Because ישראל cry out to ה׳, He saves them. This closes the readings of the פסוק in איוב with a hopeful message about ה׳'s kindness to ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ holds back His fury from ישראל. He punishes them only bit by bit, adds up even their small מצוות, and saves them when they cry out to Him.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have these words; the corrected wording adds them.

phrases.english: as a reward for crying out before Me,
I will save them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, after Steps 11 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ saves ישראל as a reward for crying out to Him.

steps.title: ה׳ takes their money to redeem them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא reads a פסוק in הושע to mean ה׳ takes ישראל's money in this world so they will merit עולם הבא, but they speak lies against Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי אבא said. What does the פסוק 'And I will redeem them, and they spoke lies against Me' mean? ה׳ says: I planned to redeem them through losing their money in this world, so they would earn עולם הבא, and they spoke lies against Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the idea that ה׳ punishes ישראל in small amounts for their own good. רבי אבא shows this idea is already hinted at in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said ה׳ punishes ישראל a little at a time. Here רבי אבא adds what that looks like: losing money in this world is a kind of 'redemption' that earns them עולם הבא. The 'lies' are ישראל complaining as if ה׳ were against them.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said; it links an earlier idea to a matching statement

phrases.english: And this is what רבי אבא said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And I will redeem them,
yet they have spoken lies against Me"?
phrases.notes: הושע 7:13

phrases.english: I said I would redeem them through their money
in this world,
so that they would earn the World to Come,
and they spoke lies against Me.
phrases.notes: The lie is saying ה׳ is angry at them, when really He is helping them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links back to רבא's idea in step 11 that ישראל are punished gently, and shows a פסוק that says the same thing.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳'s small punishments of ישראל in this world are for their benefit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 7:13 as explained by רבי אבא.

steps.title: ה׳ sends suffering to strengthen them for the next world
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי in the name of רבא reads another פסוק in הושע‎: ה׳ sends suffering in this world so ישראל's arms will be strong in עולם הבא, yet they think He is doing evil to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also matches what רב פפי said in the name of רבא. What does the פסוק 'I have trained and strengthened their arms, yet they think evil of Me' mean? ה׳ said: I planned to send them suffering in this world so their arms would be strong in עולם הבא, and they think I am doing them evil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching proof from the same chapter of הושע. This time it is about suffering (יסורין) instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יִסַּרְתִּי is read as coming from יסורין, suffering. The suffering now makes them 'stronger' later, in עולם הבא. Again ישראל misread ה׳'s kindness as harm.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: And this is what רב פפי said in the name of רבא:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Though I have disciplined and strengthened their arms,
yet they think evil of Me"?
phrases.notes: הושע 7:15

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֲיַסְּרֵם בְּיִסּוּרִין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: I said I would send them suffering in this world
so that their arms would be strong in the World to Come,
and they think I am doing evil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second parallel proof, moving from money (step 14) to bodily suffering.
steps.raayaObject: That suffering in this world is ה׳'s kindness to ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 7:15 as explained by רב פפי in the name of רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Losing money and suffering in this world are, for ישראל, a way of gaining עולם הבא, even though people often see them as signs of ה׳'s anger.

steps.title: רבי אבהו praises רב ספרא to the heretics
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רבי אבהו praised רב ספרא to the מינים as a great man, so they excused him from taxes for thirteen years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו used to praise רב ספרא to the מינים, saying he was a great man. Because of this, they let him off his taxes for thirteen years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will connect to the topic of ה׳ punishing ישראל. This step only sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background matters: the מינים trusted רבי אבהו's praise and gave רב ספרא a real benefit. That is why they later feel tricked when he cannot answer their question.

phrases.english: רבי אבהו would praise to the heretics
רב ספרא, saying that he is a great man;
so they let him off his taxes for thirteen years.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁתַּבַּח לְהוּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לְמִינֵי בְּרַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining פסוקים to a story about the same theme of ה׳ punishing ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story background: רב ספרא was praised as great and given a tax exemption.

steps.title: The heretics challenge רב ספרא with a verse
steps.stepSummary: The מינים ask רב ספרא how a פסוק in עמוס makes sense: why would ה׳ punish exactly the people He loves? He stays silent, and they torment him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day they found him and said: It is written, 'Only you have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your sins.' Does someone who is angry take it out on the one he loves? He was silent and said nothing to them. They threw a scarf around his neck and were tormenting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The מינים attack the idea that ה׳ loves ישראל, using a פסוק that seems to say love leads to punishment. רב ספרא has no answer, and they mistreat him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is logical: if you love someone, you hold your anger back from them, not pour it on them. The question fits the earlier steps, which teach that ה׳ punishes ישראל out of love, little by little.

keyTerms.meaning: I have known (I have been close to)
I will punish / call to account

steps.confusionAlert: רָחֲמֵיהּ here does not mean 'his mercy'; it means 'the one he loves,' his friend.

phrases.english: One day they found him and said to him:
It is written: "Only you have I known
of all the families of the earth;

phrases.aramaic: עַל כֵּן אֶפְקֹד עֲלֵיכֶם אֶת כׇּל עֲוֹנֹתֵיכֶם״,
phrases.english: therefore I will punish you for all your sins."
phrases.notes: עמוס 3:2

phrases.english: Someone who has anger,
does he take it out on the one he loves?

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: He was silent and said nothing at all to them.
They threw a scarf around his neck
and were tormenting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ סִיסְיָא בְּרָחֲמֵיהּ מַסֵּיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story continues: the מינים now test the 'great man' they were told about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in עמוס and the belief that ה׳ loves ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person who loves someone holds back anger from them; yet the פסוק says ה׳ punishes ישראל because He is close to them.

steps.title: The heretics complain to רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו finds them tormenting רב ספרא and asks why. They say: you told us he is great, yet he cannot even explain this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו came and found them. He said to them: Why are you tormenting him? They said: Didn't you tell us he is a great man? And he could not even tell us the meaning of this פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The story shifts to רבי אבהו, who now has to answer for his praise. The מינים challenge him, which sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their complaint is aimed at רבי אבהו's words, not just at רב ספרא. They feel the praise was false, since a 'great man' should know how to explain a פסוק.

phrases.english: רבי אבהו came and found them.
He said to them: Why are you tormenting him?
They said to him: Didn't you tell us
that he is a great man?
Yet he does not know how to tell us
the explanation of this verse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו אָמְרַתְּ לַן דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ספרא's silence, the challenge is turned on רבי אבהו's earlier praise.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's praise that רב ספרא is a great man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A truly great man would be able to explain a simple פסוק; since רב ספרא could not, the praise seems false.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: I praised him in משנה, not in verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that he praised רב ספרא as an expert in the teachings of the תנאים, not in פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Fine, I told you he was great in the teachings of the תנאים. Did I tell you he was great in פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends his praise by narrowing what he meant. He never claimed רב ספרא was an expert in explaining תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise was true, but only about one area: the teachings of the תנאים, meaning משנה and ברייתא. Not knowing how to explain a פסוק does not cancel greatness in that area. The story will continue after this.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the teachers of the משנה and ברייתא; here, their teachings

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַרִי לְכוּ בְּתַנָּאֵי,
phrases.english: He said to them: Granted, I told you [he is great] in the teachings of the תנאים;
did I tell you [he is great] in verses?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַרִי לְכוּ בְּתַנָּאֵי, בִּקְרָאֵי מִי אֲמַרִי לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the מינים' complaint about רבי אבהו's praise.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אבהו called רב ספרא great if he could not explain a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The praise was only about knowledge of the תנאים' teachings, not about explaining פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבהו is not taking back his praise. He is explaining that it was about a specific area of Torah.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the claim: the praise was only about one area of Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מינים assumed רבי אבהו's praise meant רב ספרא was great in every area, including פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The praise was about רב ספרא's knowledge of the teachings of the תנאים, so his silence on a פסוק does not make it false.

steps.title: The heretics ask why Israeli scholars know פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The מינים ask רבי אבהו what makes the scholars of ארץ ישראל different, since they know פסוקים well.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What is different about you, that you know the פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The מינים accept רבי אבהו's answer about רב ספרא and ask a follow-up question. If the scholars of בבל don't focus on פסוקים, why do the scholars of ארץ ישראל know them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו just said רב ספרא is an expert in תנאים teachings, not פסוקים. The מינים notice a contrast: רבי אבהו himself does know פסוקים. They want to know the reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The מינים are now talking to רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: What is different about you, that you know?
phrases.notes: They mean the פסוקים. They are asking why the scholars of ארץ ישראל know them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא אַתּוּן דְּיָדְעִיתוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question to רבי אבהו's defense of רב ספרא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ארץ ישראל scholars know פסוקים when the בבל scholars do not focus on them

steps.title: Living among the heretics forces deep study
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that because they live among the מינים, the scholars of ארץ ישראל push themselves to study פסוקים carefully, while the scholars of בבל do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We, who live among you, take it upon ourselves to study closely. They do not study closely.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question. Israeli scholars must debate the מינים, so they study פסוקים in depth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is need, not ability. Being near the מינים means being challenged about פסוקים all the time, so the Israeli scholars prepare. The scholars of בבל face no such debates, so they put their effort elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: we place it upon ourselves, we take on the duty

phrases.english: He said to them:
We, who are found among you —
we take it upon ourselves and study closely;
they do not study closely.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the scholars of בבל, like רב ספרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Living among the מינים forces Israeli scholars to study פסוקים deeply; the scholars of בבל have no such pressure

steps.title: The heretics ask רבי אבהו to explain the פסוק himself
steps.stepSummary: The מינים challenge רבי אבהו to explain the פסוק from עמוס that רב ספרא could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Then you tell us!
steps.whatsHappening: The מינים ask רבי אבהו to answer their question himself. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אבהו says he does study פסוקים, the מינים take him at his word. They want him to explain why ה׳ would punish the people He loves, which was the question from step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: let him tell us, tell us

phrases.english: They said to him: You tell us!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אבהו's claim into a demand to explain the עמוס פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the עמוס פסוק: why ה׳ punishes the people He loves

steps.title: The parable of the lender and his two debtors
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו compares ה׳ to a lender. From a friend he collects the debt little by little; from an enemy he collects it all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will tell you a parable. What is this like? It is like a man who lent money to two people, one his friend and one his enemy. From his friend he collects little by little. From his enemy he collects everything at once.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the hard פסוק with a parable. ה׳ punishes ישראל because He loves them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishing ישראל right away for each sin, in small amounts, is a kindness. It spares them one huge, crushing punishment. ה׳ saves up the punishment of His enemies and collects it all at once. This fits the idea from step 15 that suffering in this world helps ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ punishes ישראל because He loves them. He collects the 'debt' of sin little by little so they are never wiped out by one huge punishment.

phrases.english: He said to them: I will tell you a parable.
What is the matter like?
To a person who lent money to two people,
one his friend and one his enemy.
His friend — he collects from him little by little;
his enemy — he collects from him all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֶמְשׁוֹל לָכֶם מָשָׁל, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand of step 22 and resolves the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ punishes those He loves little by little as a kindness, while He punishes His enemies all at once

steps.title: אברהם tells ה׳ that killing the righteous with the wicked is unthinkable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא explains the word 'חלילה' in אברהם's prayer for סדום as 'חולין'. Killing the righteous together with the wicked would be a desecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: What does it mean when it is written, 'Far be it from You to do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked'? אברהם said before ה׳: Master of the world, it would be a desecration for You to do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about how ה׳ punishes. רבי אבא בר כהנא explains אברהם's words when ה׳ told him He would destroy סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא בר כהנא reads 'חלילה' as related to 'חולין', something degraded or profane. אברהם is saying that punishing the righteous along with the wicked would not fit ה׳'s justice at all. This connects to the earlier theme of how ה׳ metes out punishment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Far be it from You to do such a thing,
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:25

phrases.english: to kill the righteous with the wicked"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבְרָהָם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Abraham said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
it is a desecration to do such a thing,
phrases.notes: Here 'חלילה' is read as 'חולין', which sounds similar and means something profane.

phrases.english: to kill the righteous with the wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New aggadic teaching on the related theme of divine punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם said it would be a desecration for ה׳ to kill the righteous along with the wicked

steps.title: But a פסוק says ה׳ cuts off righteous and wicked together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the teaching: a פסוק in יחזקאל says ה׳ will cut off both the righteous and the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does He not do this? But it is written: 'And I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא בר כהנא's teaching with a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If killing the righteous with the wicked is unthinkable for ה׳, how can a פסוק in יחזקאל say ה׳ will do exactly that? The two פסוקים seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it not written? (brings a פסוק as a challenge)

phrases.english: And does He not?
phrases.notes: He means: does ה׳ really never kill the righteous with the wicked?

phrases.english: But is it not written:
"And I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked"!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 21:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא בר כהנא's claim that ה׳ does not kill the righteous with the wicked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in יחזקאל says ה׳ will cut off both the righteous and the wicked together

steps.title: The פסוק in יחזקאל means someone not fully righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'righteous' in יחזקאל is someone who is not completely righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is talking about a righteous person who is not completely righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash between the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's principle applies to a truly righteous person, who is never destroyed with the wicked. The פסוק in יחזקאל is talking about someone who is only partly righteous. Such a person can be punished along with the wicked.

keyTerms.meaning: a righteous person who is not completely righteous

steps.whatToRemember: A completely righteous person is not destroyed with the wicked. Someone who is only partly righteous can be.

phrases.english: It is talking about a righteous person who is not complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the two פסוקים speak about different kinds of righteous people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יחזקאל פסוק seemed to say ה׳ destroys even fully righteous people with the wicked
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a person who is not fully righteous is cut off with the wicked; a fully righteous person is not

steps.title: Even fully righteous people were punished at the Temple's destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a צדיק גמור is never punished together with the wicked, using רב יוסף's reading of a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it true that a completely righteous person is not punished with the wicked? It is written: 'And begin at My Sanctuary.' רב יוסף taught: Don't read it as 'My Sanctuary.' Read it as 'My sanctified ones.' These are people who kept the whole תורה, from א to ת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the last step. It says there were fully righteous people who were punished together with the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said the 'righteous' who are cut off are only people who are not fully righteous. That suggests a צדיק גמור is never cut off. But רב יוסף reads the פסוק as 'My sanctified ones,' meaning people who kept every מצוה, and ה׳ told the destroyers to begin with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't read it as ... but rather as ... (a way of reading the פסוק's letters with different vowels)
From א to ת, meaning the entire תורה

phrases.english: But with a completely righteous person, no?
But isn't it written: "And begin at My Sanctuary"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 9:6

phrases.english: And רב יוסף taught:
Do not read it as "from My Sanctuary"
but rather as "from My sanctified ones"

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁקִּיְּימוּ אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: these are people who kept the תורה
from א until ת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks what follows from the answer in Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of Step 26 that a צדיק גמור is never destroyed with the wicked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף's reading of יחזקאל 9:6 shows that people who kept the whole תורה were destroyed first.

steps.title: Those who could have protested and didn't are not fully righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'sanctified ones' could have protested against the sinners and didn't, so they count as not completely righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, since they had the power to protest and they did not protest, they are considered like righteous people who are not completely righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Those people kept the תורה, but they stayed quiet when others sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping every מצוה yourself is not enough to be a צדיק גמור if you could have stopped others from sinning. Because they failed to protest, they fit the category from Step 26: righteous, but not completely. So the rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest, to object and try to stop wrongdoing
Righteous people who are not completely righteous

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a person carries responsibility for sins of others that he could have prevented.

phrases.english: There too,
phrases.notes: Meaning in the case of the people from רב יוסף's teaching.

phrases.english: since it was in their power to protest
and they did not protest,
they are like righteous people who are not complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָיָה בְּיָדָם לִמְחוֹת וְלֹא מִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the people were not truly fully righteous
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People who kept the whole תורה are צדיקים גמורים, yet they were destroyed
steps.terutzMaskana: Failing to protest when you could makes you a righteous person who is not complete, so the rule of Step 26 holds
steps.whatToRemember: A צדיק גמור is not punished with the wicked. But someone who could protest against sin and stays silent is not counted as a צדיק גמור.

steps.title: Two verses about ה׳'s anger seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out a contradiction: one פסוק says ה׳ is angry every day, and another says no one can survive His anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא pointed out a contradiction. It is written: 'A God that is angry every day.' And it is written: 'Who can stand before His anger?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב פפא sets two פסוקים against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ is angry every day, and nobody can survive His anger, then the world should not exist. Yet it does. So the two פסוקים seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction (literally: he threw verses against each other)

phrases.english: רב פפא pointed out a contradiction. It is written:
"A God that is angry every day"
phrases.notes: תהלים 7:12

phrases.english: and it is written: "Who can stand before His anger?"
phrases.notes: נחום 1:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to ה׳'s judgment
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about ה׳'s anger
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Daily anger plus anger that no one can survive would mean the world could not exist.

steps.title: An individual versus a community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: one פסוק speaks about an individual and the other about a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is about an individual, and here it is about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's contradiction by saying each פסוק speaks about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual cannot survive ה׳'s anger. A community, with all its combined merits, can survive it, which is why ה׳ can be angry every day and the world still exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Here ... and here (each source speaks about a different case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't match the two 'כאן's to the פסוקים in the order they were quoted. 'Who can stand' is about the individual, and 'angry every day' is about the community.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, with an individual; here, with a community.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּיָחִיד, כָּאן בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of Step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק applies to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים speak about the same situation, so they clash
steps.terutzMaskana: An individual cannot withstand ה׳'s anger, but a community can

steps.title: ה׳'s anger lasts only a tiny moment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ה׳'s daily anger lasts one רגע, which is 1/53,848 of an hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'A God that is angry every day.' How long is His anger? A moment. How long is a moment? One part out of 53,848 parts of an hour. That is a moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same פסוק, 'A God that is angry every day,' to explain how long that anger lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks two questions and answers them itself. ה׳'s anger lasts a רגע, and a רגע is an extremely small piece of an hour. So His daily anger is very short.

keyTerms.meaning: A moment, here a precise tiny unit of time

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "A God that is angry every day."
And how long is His anger? A moment.
And how long is a moment?
One out of fifty thousand and three thousand
phrases.notes: Put the numbers together: 53,848 parts of an hour.

phrases.english: and eight hundred and forty-eight in an hour,
that is a moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אֵל זֹעֵם בְּכׇל יוֹם״, וְכַמָּה זַעְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the פסוק from Step 29
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s daily anger lasts one רגע, which is 1/53,848 of an hour

steps.title: Only בלעם could pinpoint that moment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that no creature can pinpoint that exact moment except בלעם הרשע, and starts quoting a פסוק about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And no creature can aim for that moment, except for בלעם הרשע, as it is written about him:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that only בלעם knew the exact moment of ה׳'s anger. The גמרא is setting up a פסוק about בלעם that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moment is so tiny that nobody can catch it. בלעם was the one exception. The proof פסוק is quoted right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: To aim for exactly, to pinpoint
בלעם the wicked, the non-Jewish prophet hired to curse the Jews

phrases.english: And no creature is able
to pinpoint that moment
except for בלעם the wicked,
as it is written about him:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין כָּל בְּרִיָּה יְכוֹלָה לְכַוֵּין אוֹתָהּ רֶגַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and leads into a proof פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only בלעם הרשע could pinpoint the exact moment of ה׳'s anger
